dati_metodo: Monte Carlo simulations of linear (OLS) models with clustered errors, G = 5 to 30 clusters, plus a Bertrand-Duflo-Mullainathan difference-in-differences replication and one empirical DID example; compares cluster-robust Wald tests with several cluster bootstrap-t methods

righe.estrazione: The txt says that Wald tests based on cluster-robust standard errors over-reject when the number of clusters is small (five to thirty), because the standard errors are biased downwards; in simulations a nominal 5% test rejects about 10% or more of the time. The wild cluster bootstrap-t brings rejection rates close to 0.05 in these linear-model simulations, but the txt also notes that bootstrap results depend on the resampling method and on discreteness, and the wild cluster bootstrap-se (not -t) under-rejects for G <= 10. The txt speaks of over-rejection of tests, not of p-values directly, and its evidence is for linear models.
righe.citazione: asymptotic tests can over-reject, however, with few (five to thirty)
righe.frase_paper: Cameron et al. (2008) show, in Monte Carlo simulations of linear models, that Wald tests based on cluster-robust standard errors over-reject with few clusters (five to thirty), and that a wild cluster bootstrap-t brings rejection rates close to the nominal 5%.
righe.frase_slide: With few clusters, cluster-robust tests over-reject; wild cluster bootstrap-t restores nominal size in simulations (Cameron et al., 2008)
righe.numero_chiave: Rejection rates of 10% with standard methods can be reduced to the nominal size of 5% (abstract); few clusters = five to thirty
righe.limiti_vs_noi: Simulations and applications are linear OLS models (mostly difference-in-differences), not logit; G between 5 and 30, while our main exit models have 41 clusters (sector x year).
righe.note: Tesi compound: (a) p-values too small = implied by over-rejection, not stated in terms of p-values; (b) 'fixes' is stronger than the txt: the wild cluster bootstrap-t brings size close to 0.05, with caveats. Narrower wording proposed.

righe.estrazione: The txt says that default OLS standard errors that ignore clustering can greatly underestimate the true standard errors, and that cluster-robust standard errors (a generalization of White's heteroskedasticity-robust estimator) allow flexible within-cluster correlation. It does not compare heteroskedasticity-robust (non-clustered) with clustered standard errors as a robustness check; the contrast it draws is default versus cluster-robust.

righe.frase_paper: Cameron et al. (2008) note that default OLS standard errors that ignore within-group dependence can greatly understate the true standard errors, which is why errors are clustered.
righe.frase_slide: Standard errors ignoring clustering can greatly understate the true ones (Cameron et al., 2008)
righe.limiti_vs_noi: Contrast is default versus cluster-robust SEs in linear models; no comparison of heteroskedasticity-robust versus clustered SEs in a logit.
righe.note: The tesi 'robust vs clustered SEs' is not the txt's contrast (default vs cluster-robust). The txt also reports this partly as established by Moulton (1986, 1990), i.e. others' point.

righe.estrazione: The txt says that default OLS standard errors that ignore clustering can greatly underestimate the true standard errors, and that with few clusters even cluster-robust standard errors are downward biased. It contrasts default with cluster-robust standard errors; it has no comparison of heteroskedasticity-robust (non-clustered) versus clustered standard errors.

righe.estrazione: The txt shows, by Monte Carlo and a replication of Bertrand, Duflo and Mullainathan (2004), that the wild cluster bootstrap-t gives rejection rates close to 0.05 with few clusters, performing well with as few as six clusters. The authors recommend it for more accurate cluster-robust inference when there are few clusters. Evidence is for linear models.

righe.frase_paper: Cameron et al. (2008) show that a wild cluster bootstrap-t gives tests of close to nominal size with few clusters, in simulations of linear models with as few as six clusters.
righe.frase_slide: Wild cluster bootstrap-t keeps test size near 5% with few clusters (Cameron et al., 2008)
righe.numero_chiave: Wild cluster bootstrap-t rejection rates about 0.05 (e.g. 0.054 at G = 5, nominal 0.05) versus 0.195 for cluster-robust at G = 5
righe.limiti_vs_noi: Linear OLS models with G = 5 to 30; our models are logit with 41 clusters, so the result is a method reference, not a test on our model.
